LABEL-CHECKING POWER TIPS

01

START WITH SERVING SIZE. Every number on the label depends on how much one serving represents.

02

COMPARE LIKE WITH LIKE. Similar serving sizes make sugar, sodium, fiber and other comparisons more meaningful.

03

CHECK ADDED SUGAR. Look specifically at the “Added Sugars” line when comparing packaged foods and drinks.

04

LOOK FOR FIBER. Fiber can be one useful clue when comparing cereals, breads and snacks.

05

WATCH SODIUM. Similar packaged foods can contain very different amounts.

06

IGNORE THE HYPE. Claims like “natural,” “multigrain” or “high protein” do not tell the whole nutrition story.

07

CHECK THE INGREDIENT LIST. Ingredients are generally listed from greatest to least by weight.
